List available filesystem/partition type modules and their weights, then exit.

Check/compare mode (implies the quiet option). After the scan is done, the resulting primary partition table is compared to the existing one. The return code of then contains the number of differences (0 if they are identical except for the boot/active flag which cannot be guessed). This option has no effect if is given on the command line.
Do not start the guessing loop. Useful if the partition table should be printed (in combination with the option) without actually scanning for partitions.
Do not skip disk read errors. If this option is given, and short disk reads or general disk read errors (EIO) are encountered, will exit. If not given, the program tries to continue.

Full scan. When a possible partition is found, normally skips all sectors this entry seems to occupy and continues the scan from the end of the last possible partition. The disk scan can take quite a while if this option is given, be patient.

Do not try to get the disk geometry from the OS. If the is no block or character device but a plain file this option should be supplied. If the file to be scanned is an image of a disk, the geometry can be given by the option.
Run interactively. Each time a possible partition is identified the user is asked for confirmation.
Quiet/no output mode. However if a logfile was specified (see option) all output is written to that file. This option overrides the interactive mode.
Be verbose. This option can be given more than once resulting in quite a lot of information.

-E.help: Do not try to identify extended partition tables. If there are extended partitions on the given device will most certainly complain about too many primary partitions because there can be only four primary partitions. Existing logical partitions will be listed as primary ones.

-L.help: List available filesystem/partition type modules and their weights, then exit.

-c.help: Check/compare mode (implies the quiet option). After the scan is done, the resulting primary partition table is compared to the existing one. The return code of then contains the number of differences (0 if they are identical except for the boot/active flag which cannot be guessed). This option has no effect if is given on the command line.

-d.help: Do not start the guessing loop. Useful if the partition table should be printed (in combination with the option) without actually scanning for partitions.

-e.help: Do not skip disk read errors. If this option is given, and short disk reads or general disk read errors (EIO) are encountered, will exit. If not given, the program tries to continue.

-f.help: Full scan. When a possible partition is found, normally skips all sectors this entry seems to occupy and continues the scan from the end of the last possible partition. The disk scan can take quite a while if this option is given, be patient.

-g.help: Do not try to get the disk geometry from the OS. If the is no block or character device but a plain file this option should be supplied. If the file to be scanned is an image of a disk, the geometry can be given by the option.

-i.help: Run interactively. Each time a possible partition is identified the user is asked for confirmation.

-q.help: Quiet/no output mode. However if a logfile was specified (see option) all output is written to that file. This option overrides the interactive mode.

-v.help: Be verbose. This option can be given more than once resulting in quite a lot of information.
